paper.title: Low-Rank Single-Index Bandits with Unknown Links: From Matrices to Tensors

settings.name_in_paper: Low-rank matrix / transformed-slice tensor single-index bandit with unknown nondecreasing link (T-ESTOR)
unmapped: reward link f is unknown (single-index model), L_f-Lipschitz and nondecreasing
each round K candidate arrays drawn iid from a known joint Lebesgue density p with bounded support (max-norm < A) and score second-moment bound M (learner knows M)
parameter is low-rank matrix or has bounded transformed-slice ranks under a known orthogonal transform U
noise has finite variance sigma^2 (only second moment), drawn from a fixed law depending on X_t
selected-design Stein signal condition mu_i >= mu_min > 0 (not known to the learner)
exact access to selected-law score functions required
settings.definition_quote: At round $t\in[T]$, $T\geq1$, the learner observes a set $\mathcal X_t=\{X_{t,a}:a\in[K]\}$ of $K\geq3$ candidates drawn iid from a known joint density $p$... selects $X_t\in\mathcal X_t$ and observes only its reward, $y_t=f(\inner{X_t}{\Theta_*})+\eta_t.$ The unknown low-rank parameter $\Theta_*$ and unknown Lipschitz link $f$ are shared across actions and rounds; $\eta_t$ is conditionally mean-zero noise with a variance bound $\sigma^2$

settings.name_in_paper: Monotone low-rank single-index bandit, disclosed linear-link Gaussian submodel (lower bound)
unmapped: link is the known linear map f(z)=beta z with mu_min <= beta <= L_f, disclosed to the learner
candidates drawn iid from a known joint density p satisfying Assumption 2.1 (bounded support, score moment bound M)
learner may also know the structural subspace used in the proof
parameter low-rank matrix or transformed-slice low-rank tensor with entrywise l1 budget B
settings.definition_quote: Fix any candidate law $p$ satisfying Assumption~\ref{ass:candidate-distribution}, retain the fresh iid menus of Section~\ref{sec:bandit-model}, and take $f(z)=\beta z$ with $0<\mu_{\min}\leq\beta\leq L_f$ and independent $\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$ noise, $\sigma^2>0$.

settings.name_in_paper: Low-rank single-index bandit with arbitrary (nonmonotone) Lipschitz link (T-BSTOR)
unmapped: reward link f unknown, L_f-Lipschitz, not necessarily monotone
nonzero base-law Stein signal |E_p f'(<X,Theta*>)| >= gamma > 0
candidates iid from a known joint density p with bounded support and score moment bound M; projection concentration certificate kappa_X known to the learner
learner knows a structural bound D >= d r (or d r_U) used for the exploration schedule
noise has only finite variance sigma^2
settings.definition_quote: We retain the parameter classes, candidate-law regularity, and finite-variance noise model of Section~\ref{sec:preliminaries}, with $f$ now any $L_f$-Lipschitz link on $[-AB,AB]$. For $\Theta_*\ne 0$, assume $|\mu_*|\geq\gamma>0$, where $\mu_*=\mathbb E_p[f'(\inner X{\Theta_*})]$.

settings.name_in_paper: Single-index bandit with arbitrary Lipschitz link, disclosed parameter, Gaussian noise (lower bound)
unmapped: parameter Theta_0 is disclosed; unknown link from a fixed class F_0 of smooth L_f-Lipschitz nonmonotone links with base Stein signal >= gamma
candidates iid from known density p satisfying the local assumptions
settings.definition_quote: Fix finite dimensions, $K\geq3$, $A,B,L_f,\sigma>0$, and $0<\gamma<L_f$, all independent of $T$... For rewards $y_t=f(\inner{X_t}{\Theta_0})+\eta_t$ with independent $\mathcal N(0,\sigma^2)$ noise

algorithms.name: T-ESTOR (Tensor Epoched Stein's Oracle Single Index Bandit)

symbols.mu_min: uniform lower bound on selected-design Stein multiplier
symbols.V: 2 L_f^2 A^2 B^2 + sigma^2 (paired reward factor)
symbols.M_score: known bound on the joint score second moment
symbols.r_U: sum of transformed-slice rank caps (r in matrix case)
symbols.q: number of transformed slices (1 for matrices)

conditions: f nondecreasing and L_f-Lipschitz
Condition 3.2: selected-design Stein signal mu_i >= mu_min > 0
Assumption 2.1 on candidate density
Theta_* != 0 (else regret zero)
exact selected-score access
tuning: Theorem 3.1 tuning for nu and lambda

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: If $\Theta_*\ne0$, then \mathbb E R_T\leq C\,\frac{L_fK}{\mu_{\min}} \sqrt{VM\norm{\Sigma_X}_{\rm op}\, r_U(d+K)T\log\!\bigl(2q(d_1+d_2)T\bigr)} = \widetilde O(\sqrt{dr_UT}), where $C>0$ is universal. ... Every policy also satisfies $\mathbb E R_T\leq2L_fABT$.

results.notes: Regret uses realized-menu best mean reward (pseudo-regret type). Appendix F gives explicit constant 100 (or 72) with min against the linear cap L_f B sqrt(K||Sigma||) T. Matrix case: r_U = r, q=1. Trivial cap 2 L_f A B T not recorded separately.

conditions: all randomized adaptive policies, which may know p, the linear link and the structural subspace
linear link f(z)=beta z with mu_min <= beta <= L_f
Gaussian noise N(0, sigma^2), sigma > 0
s_max >= 2
for every admissible candidate law p

source.label: cor:lower-large
source.quote: There is a universal $c>0$ such that, for every admissible candidate law $p$ and every integer $T\geq\max\{1,T_+(p)\}$, \inf_\pi\sup_{\Theta_*\in\mathcal C} \mathbb E_{\Theta_*,\pi}R_T \geq\frac{c\,\sigma}{K\,M\norm{\Sigma_X}_{\rm op}}\sqrt{s_{\max}\,T}.

results.notes: Minimax lower bound. T_+(p) = sigma^2 chi_lb^2 s_lb^2/(512 K^2 beta^2 B^2 M ||Sigma||^2).

bound.expression_latex: 2^{-1/4}\min\{\gamma_{\rm lb} T,\ \sqrt{\gamma_{\rm lb}\tau_{\rm lb}}\,T^{3/4},\ \tau_{\rm lb}\sqrt{s_{\rm lb}\,T}\}

symbols.gamma_lb: beta*B/(16*chi_lb*sqrt(M)), B the entrywise l1 budget
symbols.s_lb: number of mean-orthogonal rank-feasible hard directions, s_max/3 <= s_lb <= s_max
symbols.chi_lb: entrywise l1 cost of hard directions

conditions: all randomized adaptive policies; learner may know p and the subspace

s_lb >= 1

source.label: thm:lower-general
source.quote: Then for every $T\geq1$, \mathfrak R_T(\mathcal C;\beta,\sigma,p) \geq2^{-1/4}\min\bigl\{\gamma_{\rm lb} T,\ \sqrt{\gamma_{\rm lb}\tau_{\rm lb}}\,T^{3/4},\ \tau_{\rm lb}\sqrt{s_{\rm lb}\,T}\bigr\}. The bound still holds if the learner knows $p$ and the subspace used in the proof.

results.notes: Envelope lower bound; implies Theorem 3.4 for T >= T_+(p).

source.label: cor:lower-beta
source.quote: Let $p$ be the product-beta law... Then \mathfrak R_T(\mathcal C;\beta,\sigma,p) \geq\frac1{20K} \min\{\gamma_{\rm pb}T,\ \sqrt{\gamma_{\rm pb}\tau_{\rm pb}}\,T^{3/4},\ \tau_{\rm pb}\sqrt{s_{\max}T}\}.

results.notes: Specialization to product-beta design with sharper constants.

source.label: thm:nonmonotone-main
source.quote: run Algorithm~\ref{alg:nonmonotone} with a supplied bound $D\geq1$, $D\geq dr$ (matrices) or $D\geq dr_U$ ... Then \mathbb E[R_T]=\widetilde O\!\left( \big[(\kappa_X^2D)^{1/3}+1\big]T^{2/3}\right). Moreover, $R_T\leq2L_fABT$.

results.notes: Logs in dimensions and T suppressed; model constants fixed. Appendix eq. gives min{T, ...}.

symbols.Delta_gap: 2 L_f A B, max reward gap
symbols.J_bin: number of bins ceil(2 A L_f B / w_bin)
symbols.eps_pred: prediction error L_f A kappa_X e_{n0} sqrt(2 log(2KQ/delta_2))/gamma

source.label: thm:nonmonotone-upper-full
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta_1-\delta_2-\delta_3$, R_T\leq\mathcal U_T:={}\Delta n_0+\Delta\min\{Q,J_{\rm bin}k_{\rm blk}\}+16\sigma\sqrt{k_{\rm blk}J_{\rm bin}Q}+4Q\varepsilon_{\rm pred}+2GQw_{\rm bin}. Consequently, \mathbb E R_T\leq \min\{\Delta T,\ \mathcal U_T+\Delta T(\delta_1+\delta_2+\delta_3)\}.

results.notes: Holds with probability >= 1-delta_1-delta_2-delta_3; regret is realized-menu mean regret. Expected version adds Delta T(delta_1+delta_2+delta_3), capped at Delta T. sigma here is noise std bound.
